title: GST basics
question: What is GST, and do we need it?

body.normal: GST (Goods and Services Tax) is India's tax on the supply of goods and services. A business registers when its turnover crosses the threshold or when the law makes registration compulsory, for example for inter-state supplies of goods or exports under LUT.
body.simple: GST is India's sales tax. Some businesses must register for it; your project lead will confirm if yours does.
body.detail: GST replaced most indirect taxes in 2017. Registration gives the business a GSTIN, lets it charge GST on sales and claim credit for GST paid on purchases. Registration is compulsory once aggregate turnover crosses the threshold (generally ₹40 lakh for goods and ₹20 lakh for services, lower in some states) and in specific cases regardless of turnover, such as inter-state supply of goods or supplying through e-commerce operators. Exporters usually also file a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) to export without paying tax upfront. Registered businesses file regular returns such as GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B.
body.why: Whether your company must register depends on what it sells, where and how much. That is a decision your firm confirms for you.
